What is the name of the ancient Egyptian writing system that used pictorial symbols?
Hieroglyphs were the ancient Egyptian writing system that used pictorial symbols.
Which river was central to the development of ancient Mesopotamian civilization?
The Tigris and Euphrates rivers were central to the development of ancient Mesopotamian civilization.
What is the name of the first known code of laws, created in ancient Babylon?
The Code of Hammurabi is the first known code of laws, created in ancient Babylon.
Which ancient civilization built the pyramids at Giza?
The ancient Egyptians built the pyramids at Giza.
What was the primary material used for writing in ancient Sumer?
Clay tablets were the primary material used for writing in ancient Sumer.
Which ancient civilization is credited with inventing the wheel?
The ancient Sumerians are credited with inventing the wheel.
What is the name of the ancient Indus Valley city known for its advanced urban planning?
Mohenjo-Daro is the ancient Indus Valley city known for its advanced urban planning.
Which ancient civilization developed the concept of zero as a number?
The ancient Indians developed the concept of zero as a number.
What was the main purpose of the Great Wall of China during ancient times?
The main purpose of the Great Wall of China during ancient times was to protect against invasions from northern nomadic tribes.
Which ancient civilization is associated with the city of Troy?
The ancient Greeks are associated with the city of Troy, as described in Homer’s Iliad.
What is the name of the ancient Greek city-state known for its military discipline?
Sparta was the ancient Greek city-state known for its military discipline.
Which ancient civilization built the city of Machu Picchu?
The Inca civilization built the city of Machu Picchu.
What was the primary religion of ancient Egypt?
The primary religion of ancient Egypt was polytheistic, centered around gods like Ra, Osiris, and Isis.
Which ancient civilization created the Epic of Gilgamesh?
The ancient Sumerians created the Epic of Gilgamesh.
What is the name of the ancient Persian royal road that facilitated communication across the empire?
The Royal Road was the ancient Persian road that facilitated communication across the empire.
Which ancient civilization is known for its use of cuneiform writing?
The ancient Mesopotamians, particularly the Sumerians and Akkadians, are known for their use of cuneiform writing.
What was the main crop cultivated by ancient Egyptians along the Nile River?
Wheat and barley were the main crops cultivated by ancient Egyptians along the Nile River.
Which ancient civilization developed the first known calendar based on lunar cycles?
The ancient Babylonians developed the first known calendar based on lunar cycles.
What is the name of the ancient Chinese philosophy that emphasizes harmony with nature?
Daoism (Taoism) is the ancient Chinese philosophy that emphasizes harmony with nature.
Which ancient civilization is credited with the invention of paper?
The ancient Chinese are credited with the invention of paper during the Han Dynasty.
What was the function of the ziggurat in ancient Mesopotamian cities?
The ziggurat served as a temple complex dedicated to the city’s patron god in ancient Mesopotamian cities.
Which ancient civilization built the Colosseum in Rome?
The ancient Romans built the Colosseum in Rome.
What is the name of the ancient Egyptian queen who ruled as pharaoh and is known for her temple at Deir el-Bahri?
Hatshepsut was the ancient Egyptian queen who ruled as pharaoh and is known for her temple at Deir el-Bahri.
Which ancient civilization developed the concept of democracy in its city-state of Athens?
The ancient Athenians developed the concept of democracy in their city-state.
What was the primary language of the Roman Empire?
Latin was the primary language of the Roman Empire.
Which ancient civilization is known for the Nazca Lines in Peru?
The Nazca culture, a pre-Inca civilization, is known for the Nazca Lines in Peru.
What is the name of the ancient Mesopotamian god of wisdom and water?
Enki was the ancient Mesopotamian god of wisdom and water.
Which ancient civilization constructed the Stonehenge monument in England?
Neolithic Britons constructed the Stonehenge monument in England.
What was the main export of ancient Phoenician traders?
Tyrian purple dye and cedar wood were the main exports of ancient Phoenician traders.
Which ancient civilization is associated with the Terracotta Army buried with China’s first emperor?
The Qin Dynasty of ancient China is associated with the Terracotta Army buried with China’s first emperor, Qin Shi Huang.
What is the name of the ancient Greek epic poem attributed to Homer that tells the story of Odysseus’s journey home?
The Odyssey is the ancient Greek epic poem attributed to Homer that tells the story of Odysseus’s journey home.
Which ancient civilization developed the first known system of taxation?
The ancient Egyptians developed one of the first known systems of taxation, based on agricultural yields.
What was the purpose of the Rosetta Stone in understanding ancient Egyptian writing?
The Rosetta Stone provided a trilingual inscription that allowed scholars to decipher Egyptian hieroglyphs.
Which ancient civilization is known for its advanced aqueduct systems that transported water over long distances?
The ancient Romans are known for their advanced aqueduct systems that transported water over long distances.
What is the name of the ancient Indus Valley site that, along with Mohenjo-Daro, represents one of its major urban centers?
Harappa is the ancient Indus Valley site that, along with Mohenjo-Daro, represents one of its major urban centers.
Which ancient civilization is credited with the earliest known use of iron tools and weapons?
The Hittites are credited with the earliest known widespread use of iron tools and weapons.
What was the primary function of the Library of Alexandria in the ancient world?
The Library of Alexandria served as a major center of scholarship and housed hundreds of thousands of scrolls in the ancient world.
Which ancient civilization built the city of Teotihuacan, including the Pyramid of the Sun?
The Teotihuacan civilization built the city of Teotihuacan, including the Pyramid of the Sun.
What is the name of the ancient Egyptian god associated with the afterlife and mummification?
Osiris was the ancient Egyptian god associated with the afterlife and mummification.
Which ancient civilization developed the concept of the jury trial in legal proceedings?
The ancient Athenians developed the concept of the jury trial in their legal proceedings.
What was the main material used for tools and weapons in the Bronze Age?
Bronze, an alloy of copper and tin, was the main material used for tools and weapons in the Bronze Age.
Which ancient civilization is known for the development of the first known alphabet?
The Phoenicians are known for the development of the first known alphabet.
What is the name of the ancient Mesopotamian king who united Sumer and Akkad and created the first empire?
Sargon of Akkad is the ancient Mesopotamian king who united Sumer and Akkad and created the first empire.
Which ancient civilization is associated with the Olmec colossal heads found in Mesoamerica?
The Olmec civilization is associated with the colossal heads found in Mesoamerica.
What was the primary purpose of the Athenian Agora in ancient Greece?
The Athenian Agora served as a central public space for political, commercial, and social activities in ancient Greece.
Which ancient civilization developed the practice of mummification to preserve the dead for the afterlife?
The ancient Egyptians developed the practice of mummification to preserve the dead for the afterlife.
What is the name of the ancient Chinese dynasty that followed the Qin and is known for its cultural flourishing and the Silk Road?
The Han Dynasty followed the Qin and is known for its cultural flourishing and the Silk Road.
Which ancient civilization is credited with the invention of the plow, revolutionizing agriculture?
The ancient Sumerians are credited with the invention of the plow, which revolutionized agriculture in Mesopotamia.

What war ended with the Treaty of Versailles in 1919?
The Treaty of Versailles ended World War I in 1919.
Which treaty formally ended the American Revolutionary War?
The Treaty of Paris in 1783 formally ended the American Revolutionary War.
What conflict concluded with the Treaty of Westphalia in 1648?
The Thirty Years' War concluded with the Treaty of Westphalia in 1648.
Which war was ended by the Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494?
The Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494 resolved territorial disputes between Spain and Portugal following their overseas explorations, not a war, but it prevented conflict over newly claimed lands.
What war ended with the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713?
The War of the Spanish Succession ended with the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713.
Which treaty ended the Crimean War?
The Treaty of Paris in 1856 ended the Crimean War.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk in 1918?
Russia's participation in World War I ended with the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk in 1918.
Which treaty ended the Franco-Prussian War?
The Treaty of Frankfurt in 1871 ended the Franco-Prussian War.
What war was ended by the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo?
The Mexican-American War ended with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo in 1848.
Which treaty ended the Seven Years' War?
The Treaty of Paris in 1763 ended the Seven Years' War.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Nanking in 1842?
The First Opium War concluded with the Treaty of Nanking in 1842.
Which treaty ended the War of the Austrian Succession?
The Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748 ended the War of the Austrian Succession.
What war ended with the Treaty of Portsmouth in 1905?
The Russo-Japanese War ended with the Treaty of Portsmouth in 1905.
Which treaty ended the Korean War?
The Korean War ended with an armistice signed in 1953, not a peace treaty; no formal treaty has been signed to date.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Versailles in 1871?
There was no Treaty of Versailles in 1871; the Treaty of Frankfurt ended the Franco-Prussian War that year.
Which treaty ended the Punic Wars?
There was no single treaty ending the Punic Wars; the Third Punic War ended in 146 BCE with the destruction of Carthage by Rome.
What war ended with the Treaty of Kiel in 1814?
The Treaty of Kiel in 1814 ended hostilities between Denmark-Norway and Sweden during the Napoleonic Wars.
Which treaty ended the War of 1812?
The Treaty of Ghent in 1814 ended the War of 1812 between the United States and Britain.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Berlin in 1878?
The Russo-Turkish War of 1877–1878 concluded with the Treaty of Berlin in 1878.
Which treaty ended the Thirty Years' War?
The Treaty of Westphalia in 1648 ended the Thirty Years' War.
What war ended with the Treaty of Paris in 1783?
The American Revolutionary War ended with the Treaty of Paris in 1783.
Which treaty ended World War II in Europe?
Germany's unconditional surrender in May 1945 ended hostilities in Europe; no single peace treaty was signed with Germany until the Treaty on the Final Settlement with Respect to Germany in 1990.
What war ended with the Treaty of San Francisco in 1951?
The Treaty of San Francisco in 1951 formally ended World War II between Japan and most Allied powers.
Which treaty ended the Vietnam War?
The Paris Peace Accords in 1973 ended direct U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War; fighting continued until North Vietnam's victory in 1975.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Lisbon in 1668?
The Portuguese Restoration War concluded with the Treaty of Lisbon in 1668, recognizing Portugal's independence from Spain.
Which treaty ended the War of the Spanish Succession?
The Treaty of Utrecht in 1713 ended the War of the Spanish Succession.
What war ended with the Treaty of Constantinople in 1700?
The Treaty of Constantinople in 1700 ended the Russo-Turkish War of 1686–1700.
Which treaty ended the Austro-Prussian War?
The Treaty of Prague in 1866 ended the Austro-Prussian War.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Shimonoseki in 1895?
The First Sino-Japanese War concluded with the Treaty of Shimonoseki in 1895.
Which treaty ended the War of the League of Cambrai?
The Treaty of Noyon in 1516 ended the War of the League of Cambrai between France and Spain.
What war ended with the Treaty of Adrianople in 1829?
The Russo-Turkish War of 1828–1829 ended with the Treaty of Adrianople in 1829.
Which treaty ended the War of the Reunions?
The Treaty of Regensburg in 1684 ended the War of the Reunions between France and Spain.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748?
The War of the Austrian Succession concluded with the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in 1748.
Which treaty ended the Second Boer War?
The Treaty of Vereeniging in 1902 ended the Second Boer War.
What war ended with the Treaty of Kuchuk-Kainarji in 1774?
The Russo-Turkish War of 1768–1774 ended with the Treaty of Kuchuk-Kainarji in 1774.
Which treaty ended the War of the Quadruple Alliance?
The Treaty of The Hague in 1720 ended the War of the Quadruple Alliance.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Ryswick in 1697?
The Nine Years' War concluded with the Treaty of Ryswick in 1697.
Which treaty ended the War of the Spanish Armada?
There was no treaty ending the Spanish Armada conflict; the Anglo-Spanish War (1585–1604) ended with the Treaty of London in 1604.
What war ended with the Treaty of Berlin in 1885?
The Treaty of Berlin in 1885 confirmed the Congo Free State under King Leopold II of Belgium, following the Berlin Conference; it did not end a war but regulated colonial claims in Africa.
Which treaty ended the Yom Kippur War?
The Yom Kippur War ended with disengagement agreements in 1974, not a single peace treaty; Egypt and Israel later signed the Camp David Accords in 1978.
What war concluded with the Treaty of Nerchinsk in 1689?
The Sino-Russian border conflicts concluded with the Treaty of Nerchinsk in 1689, establishing the first formal border between China and Russia.
